# ngrok documentation: Gateway

> Every page in the Gateway section of the ngrok docs (256 pages). Each link points to the page's Markdown version.

## Getting Started

- [Gateway Overview](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/overview.md): Learn how ngrok's endpoints, domains, and Traffic Policy work together to secure and route traffic for APIs, devices, and private networks.
- [CLI Quickstart](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/endpoints/agent-cli-quickstart.md): Learn how to get started with the ngrok CLI to create secure tunnels from your local applications to the internet.
- [How Does ngrok's Gateway Work?](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/how-it-works.md): Learn how ngrok's global cloud service and agent software work together to provide secure ingress to your applications.
- [Points of Presence](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/points-of-presence.md): Find the codes and locations of ngrok's points of presence, and learn how to choose which ones handle traffic for your endpoints.

## Use Cases / API Gateway

- [Get Started with ngrok's API Gateway](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/api-gateway/get-started.md): Learn how to set up ngrok as an API gateway using a Cloud Endpoint that forwards traffic to internal Agent Endpoints with Traffic Policy.
- [Expose an MCP Server to ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, and Cursor](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/api-gateway/mcp-gateway.md): Give a local MCP server a public HTTPS URL that only your AI client can call, then connect ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, or Cursor.
- [Deploy a Multicloud API Gateway](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/api-gateway/multicloud.md): In this tutorial, you'll learn how to load balance API services across multiple clouds and apply common multicloud traffic patterns.
- [Using Datadog](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/api-gateway/monitor-ngrok.md): Learn how to observe your API gateway and the traffic passing through it to debug, create monitoring dashboards, and set alerts in Datadog.

## Use Cases / Device Gateway

- [Device Gateway Overview](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/device-gateway/overview.md): Use ngrok to securely connect to devices deployed in remote networks without firewall changes, VPNs, or open ports.
- [Device Gateway Quickstart](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/device-gateway/quickstart.md): Install the ngrok agent on a device, start a tunnel to a service running on it, and keep that tunnel up as a system service.
- [Device Gateway FAQ](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/device-gateway/faq.md): Find answers to common questions about the ngrok device gateway, including how it reaches remote devices and how it differs from a VPN.
- [Configure Secure Access to Remote IoT Devices](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/device-gateway/agent.md): Give partners secure access to IoT devices in a remote factory with one ngrok agent, Cloud Endpoints, and Traffic Policy.

## Use Cases / Device Gateway / Guides

- [Configure Remote Connectivity to Your IoT Devices in the Field](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/device-gateway/cloud-to-device.md): Reach cameras and sensors in remote factories from the cloud with ngrok, using Cloud Endpoints secured by OAuth and IP rules.
- [Secure Remote Access with ngrok for SSH and RDP](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/device-gateway/remote-access.md): Give technicians SSH and RDP access to devices in a remote network through one ngrok agent and TCP endpoints restricted by IP.
- [Private Connectivity to Remote IoT Devices with ngrokd](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/device-gateway/private-connectivity.md): Use ngrokd to reach IoT devices in remote networks over private endpoints, without giving those devices public URLs.
- [Fleet Management](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/device-gateway/fleet-management.md): Run thousands of devices from one ngrok account, with per-device authtokens, on-demand tunnels, and automation through the API.
- [Connect to Devices Using the Python SDK](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/device-gateway/sdk.md): Connect to devices or your device gateway by embedding connectivity directly into your application with the Python SDK.

## Use Cases / Device Gateway / Concepts

- [Device Security](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/device-gateway/security.md): Protect a device fleet with per-device authtokens, IP restrictions, and mutual TLS, and see which compliance standards ngrok meets.
- [Secure Tunnels for Devices](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/device-gateway/tunnels.md): Tunnels carry HTTP, TLS, and TCP traffic, so your SSH and RDP clients keep working. Unlike a VPN, a tunnel exposes only the service you choose.
- [Traffic Policy for Devices](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/device-gateway/traffic-policy.md): Use Traffic Policy to authenticate, rate limit, and route traffic to every device in your fleet without updating device firmware.

## Use Cases / Device Gateway / Installation Guides

- [Install ngrok on Linux](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/device-gateway/linux.md): Install the ngrok agent on a remote Linux device, enable SSH access to it, and limit who can connect with IP restrictions.
- [Install ngrok on Linux (ARM64)](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/device-gateway/arm64.md): Install the ngrok agent on a Linux ARM64 device, enable SSH access to it, and limit who can connect with a Traffic Policy.
- [Install ngrok on Raspberry Pi](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/device-gateway/raspberry-pi.md): Install the ngrok agent on a Raspberry Pi running Linux, enable SSH access to it, and limit who can connect with IP restrictions.
- [Install ngrok on Raspberry Pi OS (Formerly Raspbian)](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/device-gateway/raspbian.md): Learn how to install ngrok on a Raspberry Pi OS (formerly Raspbian) to provide secure remote access and management.
- [Install ngrok on a Remote Windows Device](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/device-gateway/windows.md): Install the ngrok agent on a remote Windows device, enable SSH access to it, and limit who can connect with IP restrictions.

## Use Cases / Site-to-Site Connectivity

- [Site-to-Site Connectivity Overview](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/site-to-site-connectivity/overview.md): Reach APIs, databases, and services in customer networks without a VPN, and find where to start with ngrok agents and Cloud Endpoints.
- [Site-to-Site Connectivity Quickstart](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/site-to-site-connectivity/quickstart.md): Get a basic site-to-site connection working in minutes by forwarding traffic from a Cloud Endpoint to a service in a remote network.
- [Connect to Your Customer's Network](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/site-to-site-connectivity/index.md): Follow an in-depth tutorial to learn how to use ngrok to remotely access APIs and DBs in your customer's network, connecting remotely without a VPN.
- [Site-to-Site Connectivity FAQ](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/site-to-site-connectivity/faq.md): Find answers to common questions about site-to-site connectivity with ngrok, from firewall changes to how you scope and revoke access.
- [Why Your Vendor Uses ngrok](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/site-to-site-connectivity/end-customers.md): Why your vendor has requested you install ngrok for site-to-site connectivity, how it works, and why it's secure.

## Use Cases / Site-to-Site Connectivity / Reliability

- [Install ngrok as a Background Service](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/site-to-site-connectivity/background-service.md): Keep your connection to a customer's network through reboots and crashes by running the ngrok agent as a system service.
- [Configure Active-Active Agent Redundancy](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/site-to-site-connectivity/redundant-agents.md): Run a second ngrok agent in a customer's network with endpoint pooling, so traffic keeps flowing if one agent goes down.

## Use Cases / Site-to-Site Connectivity / Private Addressability

- [Securely Connect to Remote Customer Networks from Your K8s Cluster](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/site-to-site-connectivity/customer-networks.md): Use the ngrok Kubernetes Operator to reach private services in a customer's network from your own cluster, without a site-to-site VPN.
- [Private Connectivity to Remote Customer Networks with ngrokd](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/site-to-site-connectivity/non-k8s-environment.md): Use ngrokd to reach services in a customer's private network from your own environment, without making those services public.

## Use Cases / Site-to-Site Connectivity / Production Ready

- [Set Up a Custom Connect URL](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/site-to-site-connectivity/custom-connect-url.md): Have your agents connect to your own hostname instead of connect.ngrok-agent.com, so customers can allowlist traffic they recognize.

## Use Cases / Webhooks to On-Prem

- [Webhooks to On-Prem](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/webhooks-to-on-prem/overview.md): Use ngrok to grant controlled, compliant access by trusted third-party webhook providers to services inside your network.
- [Webhooks to On-Prem Quickstart](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/webhooks-to-on-prem/quickstart.md): Receive webhooks at a Cloud Endpoint, verify their signatures, and forward them to a private service in your network.
- [Webhooks to On-Prem Full Tutorial](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/webhooks-to-on-prem/tutorial.md): Follow an in-depth tutorial to set up webhook verification and routing to your internal services, all managed by a single Traffic Policy.
- [Send GitHub Webhooks to On-Prem Jenkins Securely](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/webhooks-to-on-prem/github-to-jenkins.md): Verify GitHub webhook signatures at the ngrok edge and forward only genuine events to a Jenkins server behind your firewall.
- [Send GitHub Webhooks to On-Prem Argo CD Securely](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/webhooks-to-on-prem/github-to-argo-cd.md): Verify GitHub webhook signatures at the ngrok edge and forward only genuine events to Argo CD in a private Kubernetes cluster.

## Use Cases / Security Best Practices

- [Best Security Practices for Developer Productivity](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/security-dev-productivity/index.md): Put developer endpoints behind one Cloud Endpoint that your security team controls, secured with IP restrictions, JWTs, or mTLS.
- [Security Quick Wins](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/security-dev-productivity/securing-your-tunnels.md): Tighten security across your ngrok account with quick changes to how you manage authtokens, configure TLS, and sign in to the dashboard.
- [Setting Up HIPAA-Compliant ngrok Services](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/security-dev-productivity/hipaa-compliance.md): Enable HIPAA compliance on a Pay-as-you-go account, sign the BAA, and set up ngrok services that handle protected health data.
- [Secure Your Applications with OAuth 2.0](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/identity-aware-proxy/securing-with-oauth.md): Protect an ngrok endpoint with a Traffic Policy that makes visitors sign in through an OAuth provider such as GitHub or Google.
- [Secure Remote Access with ngrok for SSH and RDP](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/ssh-rdp/index.md): Set up SSH and RDP access to servers in a remote network with one ngrok agent, then add endpoint pooling and a custom connect URL.
- [Running ngrok Behind a Corporate Firewall](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/running-behind-firewalls.md): Diagnose agent connection problems behind a corporate firewall, including blocked certificate revocation checks.

## Examples

- [Gateway Examples](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples.md): Browse examples and patterns for using ngrok's Gateway including API gateway patterns, multicloud failover, and integrations.

## Examples / Secure and Control Access

- [Support Multiple Authentication Methods with Traffic Policy](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/ip-restrictions-basic-auth.md): Let requests through when they come from a trusted IP or carry valid Basic Auth credentials, and reject everything else.
- [Secure Admin Dashboards](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/lock-admin-dashboards.md): Add multiple layers of protection and authentication to your dashboards to prevent threat actors from even attempting attacks.
- [Create Secure Public Developer Environments](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/secure-developer-environments.md): Give each developer a public URL through one wildcard Cloud Endpoint, with shared policies like IP restrictions applied to all of them.
- [Validate Requests Against Identity Service](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/validate-requests-identity.md): Check each request against your own identity service with the http-request action, then use the result to authenticate or enrich it.

## Examples / Route and Shape Traffic

- [Implement the 'Front Door' Pattern](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/front-door-pattern.md): By using Cloud Endpoint and internal Agent Endpoints together, you loosely double your gateway and services for extra flexibility.
- [Multiplex to Internal Services from a Single Domain](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/multiplex.md): Dynamically serve any number of API or web app services from a single fully qualified domain name (FQDN) without complex networking configurations.
- [Microservices API Gateway](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/microservices-gateway.md): Route public API traffic to microservices in Kubernetes by path, with JWT authentication and rate limiting at one Cloud Endpoint.
- [Deploy Custom Error Pages](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/custom-error-pages.md): Instead of a blank page or HTTP error code, ensure your services automatically failover to error pages with clear details and instructions.
- [Intercept and Rewrite Headers in HTTP Redirect Responses](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/rewrite-headers-redirects.md): Rewrite redirect headers from services in a customer network, so redirects to internal hostnames still work through ngrok.
- [Route API and App Traffic by User Agent](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/route-api-app-traffic-user-agent.md): Automatically enforce the right type of AuthN and route requests to the appropriate upstream service from the same hostname and path.
- [Route to Endpoints by Geography](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/route-by-geography.md): Show users content based on their region, comply with regulations, or ensure traffic hits the nearest endpoint for the best latency.
- [Route to Services Based on OIDC Authentication](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/route-by-oidc.md): Sign users in with an OIDC provider and route them to different internal services based on the user data it returns.
- [Offload Analytics to a Self-Hosted Service](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/offload-analytics.md): Send request data to an analytics service in your own network with the http-request action, without adding code to your services.
- [Pre-Tier Requests by IP Address](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/pre-tier-requests.md): Use existing customer data and your service's pricing model to apply the proper rate limit to a user's IP address.

## Examples / Connect Apps and Services

- [Database Gateway](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/database-gateway.md): Put a database behind a Cloud Endpoint that requires mutual TLS, rate limits each client, and blocks dangerous queries.
- [Webhook Gateway](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/webhook-gateway.md): Verify webhooks from providers like Stripe, Twilio, and Slack at one Cloud Endpoint, then route each one to the service that handles it.
- [Self-Hosted PaaS Alternative Gateway](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/paas-alternative-gateway.md): Give apps on your own infrastructure the load balancing, security, and observability you'd get from platforms like Heroku or Vercel.
- [Agent-Assisted Gateway](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/agent-assisted-gateway.md): Put local services behind a Cloud Endpoint with real authentication, so AI coding tools and webhooks can reach your dev environment.
- [Use a Local LLM in Cursor with Ollama](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/cursor-local-llm.md): Give a local LLM in Ollama or LM Studio a public HTTPS URL that requires a token, then add it to Cursor as a custom OpenAI base URL.
- [Secure Your Public Minecraft Server](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/minecraft.md): Unwanted players can quickly destroy your hard work, but you can restrict access by letting in a specific set of IP addresses.
- [Securely Put Your Self-Hosted n8n Workflows Online](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/n8n.md): Get your n8n instance online to share with colleagues or receive webhook data with security measures designed for production usage.
- [Expose and Secure Your Self-Hosted Odoo Instance](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/odoo.md): Use ngrok with Odoo when you want to securely expose Odoo's services to the internet without complex network setups.
- [Ollama Remote Access: Expose and Secure Your Ollama API](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/ollama.md): Reach your self-hosted Ollama models from anywhere. Give your local LLM a stable public HTTPS URL with ngrok and lock it down with a bearer token.
- [Accelerate and Secure Your WordPress Installation](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/wordpress.md): Put a WordPress site behind ngrok for managed TLS certificates and DDoS protection, and restrict access to its admin dashboard.

## Examples / Ship Changes Safely

- [Switch Traffic Between Blue-Green Deployments](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/blue-green-deployments.md): Switch production traffic between blue and green environments with Traffic Policy, and test the new one with a request header first.
- [Distribute Traffic Between Canary Deployments](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/canary-deployments.md): Use ngrok to validate how features or versions of your services behave by distributing production traffic randomly or via a specific header.
- [Access CI/CD Deploy Previews on Secure URLs](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/ephemeral-workloads.md): Expose deploy previews and CI test environments on secure, short-lived URLs with ngrok endpoints and Traffic Policy.
- [Deploy a Consistent Maintenance Message with Traffic Policy](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/examples/maintenance-mode.md): Show a maintenance page on your endpoint with the custom-response action, without deploying a new service or changing DNS.

## Connectivity / Endpoints

- [Endpoints Overview](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/endpoints/index.md): Get started with ngrok endpoints, including how bindings control access, how the URL sets the protocol, and how policies manage traffic.

## Connectivity / Endpoints / Agent Endpoints

- [Agent Endpoints](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/endpoints/agent-endpoints.md): Compare Agent Endpoints with Cloud Endpoints, and check which protocols, bindings, and pooling options Agent Endpoints support.
- [Agent Endpoint Protocols](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/endpoints/protocols.md): Learn about the four endpoint protocols supported by ngrok: HTTP/S, TCP, and TLS, and how they determine traffic processing.
- [HTTP/S Agent Endpoints](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/endpoints/http.md): Learn how to create and configure HTTP and HTTPS endpoints with ngrok including domain configuration, TLS, and Traffic Policies.
- [TLS Agent Endpoints](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/endpoints/tls.md): Learn how to create and configure TLS endpoints with ngrok for handling encrypted TLS traffic using SNI-based routing.
- [TCP Agent Endpoints](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/endpoints/tcp.md): Learn how to create and configure TCP endpoints with ngrok for routing raw TCP traffic to your applications and services.
- [Endpoint Bindings](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/endpoints/bindings.md): Control where an ngrok endpoint can receive traffic from with public, internal, and Kubernetes bindings, with example URLs for each.
- [Public Agent Endpoints](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/endpoints/public-endpoints.md): Receive internet traffic through ngrok's points of presence with public endpoints, using a domain or TCP address for each URL.
- [Internal Agent Endpoints](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/endpoints/internal-endpoints.md): Create internal endpoints that receive traffic only from your other endpoints. Their .internal URLs are namespaced to your account.
- [Kubernetes Agent Endpoints](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/endpoints/kubernetes-endpoints.md): Learn about Kubernetes endpoints that provide secure, private connectivity to ngrok endpoints within Kubernetes clusters.

## Connectivity / Endpoints / Cloud Endpoints

- [Cloud Endpoints](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/endpoints/cloud-endpoints/index.md): Decide when to use Cloud Endpoints instead of Agent Endpoints, then create them in the ngrok dashboard or with the API.
- [Cloud Endpoints Quickstart](https://ngrok.com/docs/getting-started/cloud-endpoints-quickstart.md): Create your first Cloud Endpoint in the dashboard, forward it to an Agent Endpoint for your app, and then create one with the API.
- [How to Change a Cloud Endpoint Domain](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/endpoints/cloud-endpoints/change-domain-endpoint.md): Move an active Cloud Endpoint to a new domain by updating it with the ngrok API, so your service stays online during the change.
- [Forwarding Traffic to and Load Balancing Internal Endpoints with Cloud Endpoints](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/endpoints/cloud-endpoints/forwarding-and-load-balancing.md): Route traffic from a Cloud Endpoint to internal endpoints with Traffic Policy, then load balance across them with endpoint pools.
- [Path-Based Routing and Policy Decentralization with Cloud Endpoints](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/endpoints/cloud-endpoints/routing-and-policy-decentralization.md): Learn how to use Cloud Endpoints to route traffic by path and apply different Traffic Policies to each of your endpoints.

## Connectivity / Endpoints / Pooling & Load Balancing

- [Endpoint Pooling](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/endpoints/endpoint-pooling.md): Pool endpoints that share a URL to load balance traffic across them, and drain an endpoint from its pool when you need to stop it.
- [Load Balancing Between Multiple Clouds](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/endpoints/load-balancing-multiple-clouds.md): Share traffic between copies of a service in different clouds with endpoint pooling, using the CLI, SDKs, or Cloud Endpoints.

## Connectivity / Agents

- [ngrok Agents Overview](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/agent/index.md): Compare the four kinds of ngrok agent, see what they all have in common, and choose the right one for the service you want to put online.
- [How ngrok Agents Work](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/agent/how-it-works.md): Learn what an agent session is, how endpoints depend on it, and what happens to your traffic when an agent stops or loses its connection.
- [ngrok CLI and SDK Connectivity](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/agent/connectivity.md): Find the addresses the ngrok CLI and SDKs connect to, see how they keep a session alive, and troubleshoot a session that won't start.

## Connectivity / Agents / CLI Setup

- [Install the ngrok CLI](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/agent/install.md): Install the ngrok CLI on your platform, turn on shell tab completion, and keep the binary up to date with the built-in update command.
- [Agent Authtokens](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/agent/authtokens.md): Connect an ngrok agent to your account with an authtoken, and use ACLs to limit which endpoints each authtoken can create.

## Connectivity / Agents / Guides

- [Expose a Service with the ngrok Agent](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/agent/expose-a-service.md): Put an HTTP, TCP, or TLS service online with the ngrok agent, from your free dev domain to a reserved domain with authentication.
- [Run the ngrok CLI as a Service](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/agent/service.md): Run the ngrok CLI as an operating system service that starts on boot and restarts after a crash, then manage it remotely from the API or dashboard.
- [SSH Reverse Tunnel](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/agent/ssh-reverse-tunnel-agent.md): Put a service online through ngrok with the ssh command you already have, for systems where you can't install an agent.
- [CLI TLS Termination](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/agent/agent-tls-termination.md): Terminate TLS at the ngrok CLI rather than at ngrok's network, so traffic stays encrypted end to end all the way to your upstream service.
- [ngrok CLI Web Inspection Interface](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/agent/web-inspection-interface.md): Learn how to use the ngrok CLI web inspection interface at localhost:4040 to view HTTP requests and responses in real-time.

## Connectivity / Agents / Configuration File

- [ngrok CLI Configuration File](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/agent/config/index.md): Learn about the ngrok CLI configuration file for running multiple tunnels simultaneously and configuring advanced settings.
- [Agent Config Version 3](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/agent/config/v3.md): Reference documentation for ngrok Agent Configuration File version 3, including breaking changes, migration guide, and endpoint definitions.
- [Agent Config Version 2](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/agent/config/v2.md): Comprehensive reference documentation for ngrok Agent Configuration File version 2, including all configuration options and examples.

## Connectivity / Agents / Account and Network Controls

- [Agent API Keys](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/agent/api-keys.md): Add an API key to the agent so you can query and manage domains, endpoints, and other account resources from the command line.
- [Restrict Where Agents Connect From](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/agent/ip-restrictions.md): Restrict which IP addresses and CIDR ranges are allowed to open an agent session on your ngrok account, on top of authtoken authentication.
- [Agent Connect URLs](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/agent/connect-url.md): Point the ngrok agent at your own branded hostname instead of the default connect URL, and choose which certificate authority issues its certificate.

## Connectivity / Agents / Reference

- [ngrok Agent Command Line Interface (CLI)](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/agent/cli.md): Look up the usage, examples, and flags for every ngrok CLI command, including ngrok http, ngrok config, and ngrok service.
- [ngrok CLI API Commands](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/agent/cli-api.md): Look up the usage and flags for every ngrok api command, which manages the resources in your ngrok account from the command line.
- [ngrok CLI API](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/agent/api.md): Call the ngrok agent's local HTTP API to list and start tunnels, replay captured requests, and check the agent's status.
- [ngrok Agent Changelog](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/agent/changelog.md): Release notes for every version of the ngrok agent, covering new features, fixes, and the breaking changes between major versions.

## Connectivity / Agents / Versions

- [Upgrade to ngrok Agent v3](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/agent/upgrade-v2-v3.md): Upgrade the ngrok agent from v2 to v3, migrate your configuration file, and update scripts that still use the old flags.
- [ngrok Agent Version Support Policy](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/agent/version-support-policy.md): Learn about ngrok's version support policy including semantic versioning, release cadence, and support periods.
- [Agent Version Deprecation Notices](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/agent/deprecation-notices.md): Find out what to do after you get an agent deprecation email, including how to check your agent version and your options before the deadline.

## Connectivity / Kubernetes Operators

- [Kubernetes Operator](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/index.md): Give Kubernetes services public URLs with the ngrok Kubernetes Operator, or make services from other clusters and machines appear inside yours.
- [How the ngrok Kubernetes Operator Works](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/how-it-works.md): Learn how the ngrok Kubernetes Operator uses secure outbound connections to provide public endpoints for your Kubernetes services.
- [Kubernetes Operator Architecture](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/installation/architecture.md): Learn about the architecture of the ngrok Kubernetes Operator including controllers, control loops, and design decisions.
- [Kubernetes Operator Release Process](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/releasing.md): Learn about the ngrok Kubernetes Operator release process including Docker images, Helm charts, and semantic versioning.

## Connectivity / Kubernetes Operators / Quickstarts

- [Kubernetes Ingress Quickstart](https://ngrok.com/docs/getting-started/kubernetes/ingress.md): Learn how to get started with the ngrok Kubernetes Operator to create secure tunnels from your Kubernetes clusters to the internet.
- [Kubernetes Custom Resources Quickstart](https://ngrok.com/docs/getting-started/kubernetes/crds.md): Put a Kubernetes service online with the ngrok Kubernetes Operator's custom resources, then secure it with a Traffic Policy.
- [Kubernetes Gateway API Quickstart](https://ngrok.com/docs/getting-started/kubernetes/gateway-api.md): Use ngrok with the Kubernetes Gateway API for advanced routing, policy control, and future-proof ingress configuration.
- [Kubernetes Endpoints Quickstart](https://ngrok.com/docs/getting-started/kubernetes/endpoints.md): Connect any API or app to your Kubernetes clusters for local service projection, cross-cluster communication, and much more.

## Connectivity / Kubernetes Operators / Installation

- [ngrok Kubernetes Operator Network Egress Requirements](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/installation/network-egress.md): Learn which outbound hostnames and ports the ngrok Kubernetes Operator needs so you can allowlist it through a default-deny egress firewall.
- [How to Update the ngrok Kubernetes Operator](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/installation/update.md): Learn how to update the ngrok Kubernetes Operator to the latest version using Helm, including Gateway API CRD updates.
- [Kubernetes Operator Helm Configuration](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/installation/helm.md): Look up the default Helm values for the ngrok Kubernetes Operator, with recommended settings for scaling, region, and watched namespaces.
- [Monitoring the Kubernetes Operator](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/installation/observability.md): Collect the metrics the ngrok Kubernetes Operator exposes, and change its log level through Helm when you need to troubleshoot it.
- [Uninstalling the ngrok Kubernetes Operator](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/installation/uninstall.md): How to uninstall the ngrok Kubernetes Operator, clean up resources, and understand what happens during the process.

## Connectivity / Kubernetes Operators / Load Balancing

- [Load Balancing for Kubernetes Services](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/load-balancing/load-balancing-kubernetes.md): Share traffic between Kubernetes services in different clusters or clouds by pooling two Agent Endpoints with the same URL.
- [Load Balancing Between Multiple Kubernetes Clusters](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/load-balancing/load-balancing-kubernetes-clusters.md): Use Endpoint Pooling to split traffic between any number of clusters without needing to deploy external services.

## Connectivity / Kubernetes Operators / How-to

- [Controlling Traffic Flow with Request Routing](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/how-to/request-routing.md): Configure request routing in Kubernetes to direct incoming traffic to the appropriate backend services based on rules.
- [TLS Routing](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/how-to/tls-routing.md): Route encrypted traffic by SNI in Kubernetes with a TLSRoute, so it reaches the right service without the gateway decrypting it.
- [TCP Routing](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/how-to/tcp-routing.md): Route TCP traffic for databases and other non-HTTP services in Kubernetes with an AgentEndpoint, CloudEndpoint, and TCPRoute.
- [Customizing Requests with Header Manipulation](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/how-to/manipulate-headers.md): Learn how to add, modify, or remove HTTP headers in Kubernetes to enhance security, routing, and service compatibility.
- [Managing Traffic with Redirects](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/how-to/redirects.md): Configure URL redirects in Kubernetes to route users to the correct destination and enforce HTTPS connections.
- [Customizing Request Routing with URL Rewriting](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/how-to/rewrite-url.md): Rewrite the path, path prefix, or port of requests in Kubernetes with an NgrokTrafficPolicy or a Gateway API URLRewrite filter.
- [Serving Static Responses with Custom Response Policies](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/how-to/static-response.md): Configure static responses in Kubernetes to return predefined responses directly from the gateway without backend calls.
- [Managing TLS Termination for Secure Connections](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/how-to/terminate-tls.md): Configure TLS termination in Kubernetes to use custom certificates, enforce TLS versions, and enable mutual TLS.
- [Securing Upstream Connections with TLS and Mutual TLS (mTLS)](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/how-to/upstream-tls.md): Configure upstream TLS and mutual TLS in Kubernetes to secure connections between ngrok and your backend services.
- [Protecting Services with Rate Limiting](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/how-to/rate-limiting.md): Configure rate limiting in Kubernetes to protect your services from excessive traffic and ensure fair usage across clients.
- [Protecting Your Endpoints by Denying Unwanted Traffic](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/how-to/deny-requests.md): Configure request denial rules in Kubernetes to block unwanted or malicious traffic before it reaches your upstream services.
- [Securing Endpoints with Basic Authentication](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/how-to/basic-auth.md): Learn how to secure your Kubernetes endpoints with basic authentication using the ngrok Kubernetes Operator and Traffic Policies.
- [Securing Your Endpoints with OAuth Authentication](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/how-to/oauth.md): Configure OAuth authentication in Kubernetes to secure your endpoints by requiring valid OAuth tokens before forwarding requests.
- [Authenticating Users with OpenID Connect (OIDC)](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/how-to/oidc.md): Configure OpenID Connect authentication in Kubernetes to secure your endpoints using trusted identity providers.
- [Securing Your Endpoints with JWT Validation](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/how-to/jwt-validation.md): Configure JWT validation in Kubernetes to secure your endpoints by verifying authentication tokens at the network edge.
- [Controlling Access with IP Restrictions](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/how-to/restrict-ips.md): Configure IP restrictions in Kubernetes to allow or deny access based on source IP addresses using allow lists or deny lists.
- [Restricting Access by Kubernetes Pod Identity](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/how-to/pod-identity.md): Use the namespace, name, or annotations of the calling pod to decide which pods may open connections to a Kubernetes-bound endpoint.
- [Circuit Breaking for System Reliability](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/how-to/circuit-breaking.md): Configure circuit breaking in Kubernetes to protect your services from overload and maintain system reliability with ngrok.
- [Improving Performance with Response Compression](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/how-to/compress-response.md): Enable response compression in Kubernetes to improve performance and reduce bandwidth usage for your ngrok endpoints.

## Connectivity / Kubernetes Operators / Custom Resources

- [Kubernetes Operator Custom Resources (CRDs)](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/crds/index.md): Reference documentation for all custom resource definitions available in the ngrok Kubernetes Operator for managing endpoints and configurations.
- [AgentEndpoint](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/crds/agentendpoint.md): Reference documentation for the AgentEndpoint Kubernetes custom resource for managing agent-based endpoints with the ngrok operator.
- [CloudEndpoint](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/crds/cloudendpoint.md): Reference documentation for the CloudEndpoint Kubernetes custom resource for creating persistent, always-on Cloud Endpoints.
- [NgrokTrafficPolicy](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/crds/ngroktrafficpolicy.md): Reference documentation for the NgrokTrafficPolicy Kubernetes custom resource for defining reusable Traffic Policy configurations.
- [BoundEndpoint](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/crds/boundendpoint.md): Reference documentation for the BoundEndpoint Kubernetes custom resource for managing cross-cluster networking with ngrok.
- [Domain](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/crds/domain.md): Reference documentation for the Domain Kubernetes custom resource for managing reserved hostnames for ngrok endpoints.
- [KubernetesOperator](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/crds/kubernetesoperator.md): Look up every field of the KubernetesOperator custom resource, which the Helm install creates to register your Operator with ngrok.
- [IPPolicy](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/crds/ippolicy.md): Look up every field of the IPPolicy custom resource, which allows or denies traffic to your ngrok endpoints by source IP or CIDR range.

## Connectivity / Kubernetes Operators / Guides

- [Running Multiple ngrok Operator Installations](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/multiple-installs.md): How to run multiple instances of the ngrok Kubernetes Operator in a single cluster using namespace-scoped installations.
- [Running a Local Kubernetes Cluster](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/local-cluster.md): Learn how to set up a local Kubernetes cluster for development and testing with the ngrok Kubernetes Operator.
- [Using ngrok Custom Resources](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/using-crds.md): These examples show how to configure the AgentEndpoint, CloudEndpoint, and NgrokTrafficPolicy custom resources in the ngrok Kubernetes Operator.
- [How to Create Endpoints in the ngrok Kubernetes Operator](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/endpoint-types.md): Learn how to create endpoints that accept `http://`, `https://`, `tcp://`, and `tls://` requests using the ngrok Kubernetes Operator.
- [Binding Endpoints in the ngrok Kubernetes Operator](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/bindings.md): Use public, internal, and Kubernetes bindings on Operator endpoints, and restrict which pods can reach a Kubernetes-bound endpoint.
- [Pooling Endpoints in the ngrok Kubernetes Operator](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/pooling.md): Turn on endpoint pooling for each kind of ngrok Kubernetes Operator resource without accidentally pooling with endpoints you started elsewhere.
- [Kubernetes Custom White-Label Domains](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/custom-domain.md): Use your own domain with the ngrok Kubernetes Operator, with DNS records created by ExternalDNS or managed by hand.
- [Projecting Local Services into Remote Clusters](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/local-projection.md): Learn how to use Kubernetes bindings to instantly test local services against remote staging or production-like clusters without slow CI/CD loops.
- [Gateway API with the ngrok Kubernetes Operator](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/using-gwapi.md): Learn how to use Gateway API resources with the ngrok Kubernetes Operator to configure ingress and routing for your services.
- [How the ngrok Operator Uses Ingresses](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/using-ingresses.md): Attach an NgrokTrafficPolicy to an Ingress, avoid Ingress conflicts, and see how the Operator turns each Ingress host into a CloudEndpoint.
- [Migrate from ingress-nginx to the ngrok Kubernetes Operator](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/migrate-from-ingress-nginx.md): Move your Kubernetes Ingress traffic from the retired ingress-nginx controller to the ngrok Kubernetes Operator without downtime.
- [Custom ngrok Annotations](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/annotations.md): Look up the ngrok.com annotations you can add to Ingress, Gateway, and Service resources, and the legacy k8s.ngrok.com keys they replace.
- [ngrok Kubernetes Operator Managed Resources](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/managed-resources.md): Find the labels the ngrok Kubernetes Operator puts on resources it creates, so you can tell them apart from resources you manage.
- [Finalizers Created by the ngrok Kubernetes Operator](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/finalizers.md): Learn about how the ngrok Kubernetes Operator uses finalizers to ensure proper cleanup of ngrok resources before deletion.
- [Troubleshooting the ngrok Kubernetes Operator](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/troubleshooting.md): Learn how to troubleshoot common issues with the ngrok Kubernetes Operator using kubectl describe, events, and logs.
- [Exposing the Kubernetes API Server with the ngrok Operator](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/expose-kubernetes-api.md): Reach your cluster's API server with kubectl from anywhere through the ngrok Operator, using token or client certificate authentication.
- [How the ngrok Operator Uses LoadBalancer Services](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/k8s/guides/using-loadbalancers.md): Learn how the ngrok Kubernetes Operator automatically exposes LoadBalancer services using TCP or TLS endpoints with reserved addresses.

## Traffic Policy

- [Traffic Policy Overview](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/index.md): Learn about ngrok's Traffic Policy for authenticating requests, rate limiting traffic, rewriting URLs, and applying security controls.
- [How Traffic Policy Works](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/how-it-works.md): Learn how Traffic Policy phases, rules, and actions fit together, and how ngrok decides which rules run and in what order.

## Traffic Policy / Quickstarts

- [Agent Endpoints with Traffic Policy Quickstart](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/getting-started/agent-endpoints.md): Attach a Traffic Policy to an Agent Endpoint with a policy file or the agent configuration file, then send a test request.
- [Cloud Endpoints with Traffic Policy Quickstart](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/getting-started/cloud-endpoints.md): Learn how to create Cloud Endpoints with Traffic Policies using the ngrok API for programmatic endpoint management.

## Traffic Policy / Concepts

- [Expression Examples](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/concepts/expressions.md): Learn how to write CEL expressions in Traffic Policy to define conditions for triggering actions based on traffic attributes.
- [Actions](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/concepts/actions.md): Learn about Traffic Policy Actions that define what happens when rules are matched, including traffic manipulation and routing Actions.
- [Traffic Identities](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/identities.md): View and revoke the sessions of users who signed in to your endpoints with OAuth, OpenID Connect, or SAML, from the dashboard or the API.

## Traffic Policy / Actions

- [Traffic Policy Actions](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/index.md): Browse every Traffic Policy action and its type name, from authentication and rate limiting to routing and header changes.
- [Add Headers Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/add-headers.md): Use the add-headers action to attach details such as the client IP to requests and responses as they pass through your endpoint.
- [Basic Auth Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/basic-auth.md): Protect an endpoint with a username and password using the basic-auth Traffic Policy action, and configure the credentials it accepts.
- [Circuit Breaker Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/circuit-breaker.md): Prevent overload and maintain system reliability by rejecting requests when errors and volume exceed set thresholds.
- [Close Connection Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/close-connection.md): Use the close-connection action to drop client connections that match a condition, such as clients that exceed a rate limit.
- [Compress Response Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/compress-response.md): Use the compress-response action to compress response bodies with gzip, Brotli, or another algorithm the client supports.
- [Custom Response Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/custom-response.md): Use the custom-response action to answer requests directly from ngrok with your own status code, headers, and body.
- [Deny Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/deny.md): The Deny action enables you to reject incoming requests on your endpoints before they make it to your upstream service.
- [Forward Internal Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/forward-internal.md): Route requests to an internal endpoint with the forward-internal action, and decide what happens when that endpoint is offline.
- [HTTP Request Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/http-request.md): Call another service in the middle of a request with the http-request action, and configure its retries, timeouts, and error handling.
- [JWT Validation Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/jwt-validation.md): Configure the jwt-validation action, including the issuer, audience, and signing keys a token must match to reach your service.
- [Log Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/log.md): Use the log action to record custom metadata, including values built with CEL interpolation, when a Traffic Policy rule runs.
- [OAuth Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/oauth.md): The OAuth action restricts access to only authorized users by enforcing OAuth through an identity provider of your choice.
- [OpenID Connect Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/openid-connect.md): The OpenID Connect (OIDC) action restricts access to only authorized users by enforcing OIDC through an identity provider of your choice.
- [OWASP CRS Request Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/owasp-crs-request.md): Use the owasp-crs-request action to block SQL injection, cross-site scripting, and other common attacks in incoming requests.
- [OWASP CRS Response Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/owasp-crs-response.md): Use the owasp-crs-response action to catch leaked error messages and sensitive data in responses before they reach clients.
- [Rate Limit Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/rate-limit.md): Use the rate-limit action to cap how many requests reach your endpoint, either overall or per client IP, header, or other key.
- [Redirect Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/redirect.md): Redirect clients to a new host or path with the redirect action. For changes the client shouldn't see, use the url-rewrite action instead.
- [Remove Headers Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/remove-headers.md): Use the remove-headers action to keep sensitive or unneeded headers from reaching your upstream service or your clients.
- [Request Body Find and Replace Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/request-body-find-replace.md): Configure the request-body-find-replace action, with examples that redact sensitive data and modify AI prompts in requests.
- [Response Body Find and Replace Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/response-body-find-replace.md): Configure the response-body-find-replace action, with examples that redact sensitive data and add disclaimers to AI responses.
- [Restrict IPs Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/restrict-ips.md): Block or allow connections to your endpoint by IP with the restrict-ips action, using CIDR lists or existing IP Policies.
- [SAML Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/saml.md): The SAML action restricts access to only authorized users by enforcing SAML through an identity provider of your choice.
- [Set Vars Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/set-vars.md): Use the set-vars action to store values, including ones built with CEL interpolation, that later rules and expressions can read.
- [SSE Find and Replace Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/sse-find-replace.md): Configure the sse-find-replace action, with examples that redact sensitive data and filter profanity in streaming AI responses.
- [Terminate TLS Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/terminate-tls.md): Use the terminate-tls action to set minimum and maximum TLS versions, serve a custom certificate, or require mutual TLS.
- [URL Rewrite Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/url-rewrite.md): Change the path or query of a request before it reaches your service with the url-rewrite action. To send the client elsewhere, redirect instead.
- [Verify Webhook Action](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/actions/verify-webhook.md): Reject webhooks with invalid signatures or old timestamps using the verify-webhook action, and check which webhook providers it supports.

## Traffic Policy / Examples

- [Traffic Policy Examples](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/examples/index.md): Browse Traffic Policy examples for common jobs like routing requests, requiring authentication, and filtering traffic by IP or user agent.
- [How to Run an A/B Test](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/examples/a-b-tests.md): Learn how to run A/B tests using Traffic Policy by routing traffic to different endpoints based on random distribution.
- [Add and Remove Headers](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/examples/add-and-remove-headers.md): These examples show how to add client details to requests, strip server details from responses, and mark an API version as deprecated.
- [Add Authentication](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/examples/add-authentication.md): Learn how to add authentication to your endpoints using Traffic Policy with Basic Auth, OAuth, OIDC, JWT validation, and more.
- [Block Unwanted Requests](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/examples/block-unwanted-requests.md): Learn how to block unwanted or malicious requests using Traffic Policy including examples for blocking Tor, bots, and specific IPs.
- [Filter Traffic by IP Category](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/examples/filter-by-ip-category.md): Block AI crawlers, Tor exit nodes, and known threats, or allow only one cloud provider, with ngrok's IP Intelligence categories.
- [Compress JSON Responses Example](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/examples/compress-json-responses.md): This example shows how to compress JSON responses from your upstream service with Traffic Policy, and what happens if they're already compressed.
- [Enforce TLS Example](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/examples/enforce-tls.md): Learn how to enforce minimum TLS version requirements using Traffic Policy to reject connections using outdated TLS versions.
- [Event Logging Example](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/examples/event-logging.md): Learn how to configure event logging in Traffic Policy to export logs to external services like Datadog for monitoring and troubleshooting.
- [Using OAuth Traffic Policy on Endpoints](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/examples/oauth-protection.md): Make visitors sign in with Google, GitHub, or another provider before they reach your endpoint, and allow only certain email addresses.
- [How to Rate Limit Traffic](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/examples/rate-limit-requests.md): Learn how to rate limit requests using Traffic Policy with examples for endpoint-based, IP-based, and key-based rate limiting.
- [Route Requests](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/examples/route-requests.md): Send requests to different internal endpoints with Traffic Policy based on the subdomain, path, headers, or other request details.
- [URL Rewrites Examples](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/examples/url-rewrites.md): Learn how to rewrite URLs using Traffic Policy to map user-friendly URLs to backend permalinks for better SEO and user experience.
- [User Agent Filtering Example](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/traffic-policy/examples/user-agent-filtering.md): This example shows how to match on the browser or bot in a request's User-Agent header to serve different content or block unwanted crawlers.

- [Global Load Balancer](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/domains/global-load-balancer.md): Learn about ngrok's Global Load Balancer for distributing traffic to the nearest healthy point of presence for improved performance.

## Identity & Access

- [Identity and Access Management Overview](https://ngrok.com/docs/iam/index.md): Learn about ngrok's identity and access management system for managing credentials, enforcing access controls, and federating identity.

## Identity & Access / Principals

- [Users](https://ngrok.com/docs/iam/users.md): Understand how users work in ngrok accounts including authentication, credentials, dashboard access, and multi-account membership.
- [Service Users](https://ngrok.com/docs/iam/service-users.md): Service Users are ngrok service accounts that own credentials independently of a person, so automated systems keep working when people leave.

## Identity & Access / Account Governance

- [Single Sign-On and Provisioning to the ngrok Dashboard](https://ngrok.com/docs/iam/sso.md): Learn how to configure single sign-on for the ngrok dashboard using SAML or OpenID Connect identity providers.
- [Role-Based Access Control](https://ngrok.com/docs/iam/rbac.md): Configure role-based access control in ngrok to restrict actions that users and service users can perform in your account.
- [Account Domain Controls](https://ngrok.com/docs/iam/domain-controls.md): Keep everyone at your organization in one ngrok account with single sign-on by verifying your email domain, and see what changes for users.
